findings.title: impersonation-domain
findings.explanation: Unapproved host astralharb0r.test resolves in the pinned snapshot and holds a matching certificate. The captured page copies the official tag sequence and DOM text, but its contract and spender literals are outside the approved address registry. Its WalletConnect projectId is also off-registry. All signals sit on one host, so they form one finding. The blocklist match is the synthetic lab list, not a vendor detection. A similar name and a certificate do not prove criminal ownership. Fix: Review ownership of astralharb0r.test, block it at the proxy and link registry, and pursue an authorized takedown. Do not claim or register the domain.

proof.detail: Allowlisted detector confirmed the pinned evidence.

findings.title: lookalike-identity
findings.explanation: A support identity astralharb0r_help resembles the approved handle but is not in the registry. Its support text requests recovery material. Only pinned profile fields were compared and no account was contacted. A similar handle does not prove malicious ownership. Recovery phrases must never be shared, even with an approved support contact. Fix: Pin the approved support handle in the registry, point official support links only at it, and pursue an authorized takedown of the lookalike if ownership review confirms it is unapproved.

proof.detail: Allowlisted detector confirmed the pinned evidence.

findings.title: github-two-factor-not-required
findings.explanation: The pinned organization export fails the Legitify policy two_factor_authentication_not_required_for_org. This proves only the exported setting, and the exported value shows 2FA not required at the organization level. Missing export fields would not be treated as proof of a disabled control. Fix: Enforce required 2FA at the organization level, then re-run the pinned export to verify the exported setting.

proof.detail: Allowlisted detector confirmed the pinned evidence.

findings.title: impersonation-domain
findings.explanation: The Unicode homograph xn--astralhrbor-4ij.test resolves in the pinned snapshot and holds a matching certificate. A captured off-brand page advertises the project plus a claim or airdrop absent from the approved campaign registry. A similar name and a certificate do not prove criminal ownership. Three script names match a published Inferno pattern, but names alone do not prove malware and that signal is review-only, so it is not the root cause. Fix: Review ownership of xn--astralhrbor-4ij.test, block the host, withdraw or reconcile the unapproved claim/airdrop offer, and pursue an authorized takedown. Do not claim or register the domain.

proof.detail: Allowlisted detector confirmed the pinned evidence.

findings.title: address-poisoning-docs
findings.explanation: The published document at astralharbor.test/docs/treasury shows an address that differs from the approved address but shares its first six and last four hex digits. That pattern can mislead visual copying of addresses. No transfer or chain lookup was made. Fix: Correct the document to the approved address and add a pre-publish check that flags addresses sharing a first/last digit pattern with approved addresses.

findings.explanation: The official support page contains a link labeled as an official brand destination that points to astralharb0r.test/support. Fix: Repoint the link to the approved support domain and add a link-registry check to the publishing pipeline so off-registry targets are flagged.
